## Goal
- Convertir Acoustical (app Android Kotlin/Compose, `com.rork.acoustical`) en controladora profesional de audio; fase actual: **build del plan "124 bandas, EQ L/R independiente, multiruta y Ruteos con entradas"** (`.rork/plans/acoustical-124-bandas-eq-l-r-independien_1788270713262.plan.md`) — cambios casi todos aplicados, falta validar compilación.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Android nativo (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose); Mac app y VST fuera de alcance
- Paleta Deep Ocean (negro abisal, teal, cian, ámbar/lima); UI en español, compacta
- **NO joystick circular**: pad de 4 botones tipo teclado; 2 faders verticales sensibles; 4 botones L/Mid/R/Lados con un solo envío
- Agente ingeniero 4 modos; protecciones críticas SIEMPRE activas; pre-flight "va a sonar" antes de des-silenciar
- Distancias GPS: ESCALA pulsado=0.5m, suelto=0.01m; automatiza delay+ganancia
- Specs: 96 kHz, SPL 97 dB, delay 25.0–2000.0 ms, 16/24/32-bit float
- **124 bandas de EQ** (nueva opción "124 · Ultra", frecuencias log 20 Hz–20 kHz)
- **Ganancia máxima de corrección: 50 dB** (slider 0–50)
- **Retardos en pasos de 0.01 ms** siempre con doble lectura tiempo+distancia ("12.45 ms · 4.27 m", cm si <1 m; 34.3 cm/ms)
- **Suavizado extendido automático** cuando maxGainDb > 24 (factor escalado ×24/max, min 0.05) + aviso en Ajustes
- **Multiruta**: cada salida suena a la vez por su propio dispositivo físico con señal distinta (elección del usuario: "independent")
- **Ruteos simplificado**: dos columnas conectadas (entruestas ⇄ salidas), entradas gestionables
- **EQ con Link/Unlink L y R** ajustables por separado
- **Auto-corrección**: 2 bandas por ciclo (la más alta y la más baja desviadas), 2 veces por segundo (500 ms)
- Validación final en **Redmi Note 15 4G físico del usuario** (no accesible; usuario prueba y reporta)

## Progress
### Done
- Plan creado y actualizado con delay fino + suavizado + validación; usuario aprobó ("Build the plan")
- **AudioModels.kt**: `BandCount.BAND_124(124, "124 · Ultra")`, labels cortos; `StandardFrequencies.ultra124` (124 log-spaced 20–20k, ratio 1000^(1/123)); `AudioConfig.effectiveSmoothingFactor` + `needsExtendedSmoothing`; `EqBand.isClampedAt(maxGainDb)` sustituye a `isClamped` fijo
- **RoomCorrector.kt**: corrección rápida de 2 bandas — `TWO_BAND_PERIOD_MS=500`, `computeCorrections` corrige simultáneamente banda más desviada (+) y más deficitaria (−) máximo 2×/s; `bandEdgeRatio` 1/12 octava si bandCount>40; `correctionIntensity` normalizada a 2×maxGain; `reset()` limpia `lastCorrectionMs`
- **AudioEngine.kt**: RoomCorrector usa `effectiveSmoothingFactor`; `setBandGain` clampea a `±config.maxDb` (ya no ±12 fijo)
- **TestSignal.kt REESCRITO (multiruta)**: HashMap `activeTracks` por outputId (señales simultáneas); `play(outputId, type, durationMs, volume, gainDb, delayMs, isMuted, device: AudioDeviceInfo?, onFinished)`; `track.preferredDevice = device` para rutear a altavoz/BT/USB/wired; `stop(outputId)` individual y `stopAll()`; delay cuantizado a muestras 48 kHz; `activeOutputIds` expuesto
- **ControllerModels.kt**: `InputType` (MIC/USB/CONSOLE_IN/FILE_REFERENCE) + `InputTarget` (id, type, name, isActive, gainDb, subtitle); `EqChannel` (LEFT/RIGHT)
- **AudioEngineViewModel**: UiState — `routingNodes`/`routingConnections` eliminados, nuevos `inputs: List<InputTarget>`, `testingOutputIds: Set<String>`, `bandsL`/`bandsR`, `eqLinked`, `eqChannel`; `initRoutingNodes()`→`initInputs()`, `updateRoutingNodes()`→`updateInputs()` (replaceAll); `toggleInputActive`, `setInputGainDb(±12)`; `playTestSignal` multiruta con `resolveOutputDevice(type)` (TYPE_BUILTIN_SPEAKER/BLUETOOTH_A2DP/USB_*/WIRED_*); `stopTestSignal(outputId?)` con null=all; `setEqBandGain(channel, index, gain)` con offsets por canal (eqOffsetsL/R) sobre ganancia del motor, `setEqLinked`, `toggleEqLink`, `setEqChannel`, `setBandGain` legacy = linked; `resetBands` limpia offsets; `loadProfile` resetea offsets y copia a L/R; `setOutputDelayMs` redondea a 0.01 ms + `nudgeOutputDelay`; `setAudioDelayMs` redondea 0.01 ms sin restart + `nudgeAudioDelay`; `setOutputGainDb` clampea a ±maxGainDb; `stopAll` en onCleared; mesh publish llama `publishChannelBands()`; auto-check loop simplificado llama `updateInputs()`
- **FineDelayControl.kt (nuevo, ui/components/)**: slider + botones finos ±0.01 ms, lectura "%.2f ms · distancia" (`formatDelayDistance`, 0.343 m/ms)
- **EqSliders.kt**: `EqSliderRow` scrollable horizontal si >10 bandas; nuevo `EqChannelBar` (chips L/R deshabilitados si link + chip Link/Unlink)
- **FullEqScreen.kt / EqualizerScreen.kt**: EqChannelBar + sliders de canal activo (`bandsL`/`bandsR`) vía `setEqBandGain(state.eqChannel, ...)`; subtitle EQ muestra "%.2fms"
- **SettingsScreen.kt**: chips de bandas en horizontal scroll (con 124) + contador; slider maxGain 0–50 (steps 49); FineDelayControl para retardo global (25–2000); aviso ámbar de sujetetado efectivo si needsExtendedSmoothing

## Key Decisions
- Multiruta: un AudioTrack por outputId con `preferredDevice` → altavoz + BT suenan a la vez con señ distintas (elección "independent" del usuario)
- EQ L/R: offsets manuales por canal (`eqOffsetsL/R`) sobre la ganancia automática del motor; auto-corrección sigue afectando a ambos canales; link aplica el mismo offset a ambos
- Auto-corrección: sustituye al cálculo continuo; máx 2 bandas/cada 500 ms, normal + clamp ±maxGainDb + suavizado
- Retardo: UI en pasos de 0.01 ms; reproducción cuantizada a muestras enteras 48 kHz (1 muestra ≈ 0.021 ms)
- Ruteos: sin Canvas mapa de nodos de proceso; `setAudioDelayMs` ya no reinicia engine (afecta test/UI)
- Suavizado: `effectiveSmoothingFactor` en AudioConfig (factor × 24/maxGainDb sobre 24 dB, mínimo 0.05)
- testingOutputId (singular) → `testingOutputIds` (Set) para permitir pruebas simultáneas

    10|/**
    11| * Analyzes the difference between a reference spectrum (what the source sends)
    12| * and the measured spectrum (what the microphone receives in the room),
    13| * then computes EQ band gains to compensate for room-induced coloration.
    14| *
    15| * The algorithm:
    16| * 1. Aggregate FFT bins into 1/N-octave bands centered on standard frequencies.
    17| * 2. Compute the deviation: measured - reference for each band.
    18| * 3. Invert the deviation to produce correction gains (negative gain for peaks,
    19| *    positive gain for dips).
    20| * 4. Apply smoothing and clamping to avoid oscillation and extreme boosts.
    21| */
    22|class RoomCorrector(
    23|    private val bandFrequencies: FloatArray,
    24|    private val sampleRate: Int,
    25|    private val fftBinCount: Int,
    26|    private val maxGainDb: Float,
    27|    private val smoothingFactor: Float,
    28|    private val noiseFloorDb: Float
    29|) {
    30|
    31|    private val bandCount: Int = bandFrequencies.size
    32|    private val previousGains = FloatArray(bandCount)
    33|    private var currentBandLevels = FloatArray(bandCount)
    34|
    35|    /** Fast two-band correction cadence: 2 corrections per second (500 ms). */
    36|    private var lastCorrectionMs = 0L
    37|
    38|    /**
    39|     * Band edge ratio for aggregation. With ultra band counts (124) the
    40|     * spacing is ~1/12 octave, so narrower edges avoid heavy overlap.
    41|     */
    42|    private val bandEdgeRatio: Double =
    43|        if (bandCount > 40) 2.0.pow(1.0 / 12.0) else 2.0.pow(1.0 / 6.0)
    44|
    45|    /**
    46|     * Aggregate raw FFT bins into perceptual bands using log-spaced center frequencies.
    47|     *
    48|     * @param magnitudesDb dB magnitudes from the FFT (size = fftBinCount)
    49|     * @param binFrequencies frequency in Hz for each FFT bin
    50|     * @return array of averaged dB levels per band
    51|     */
    52|    fun aggregateBands(
    53|        magnitudesDb: FloatArray,
    54|        binFrequencies: FloatArray
    55|    ): FloatArray {
    56|        val bandLevels = FloatArray(bandCount)
    57|
    58|        for (b in 0 until bandCount) {
    59|            val center = bandFrequencies[b]
    60|            // Band edges: half the band spacing (1/3 or 1/6 octave depending on density)
    61|            val ratio = bandEdgeRatio
    62|            val lower = (center / ratio).toFloat()
    63|            val upper = (center * ratio).toFloat()
    64|
    65|            var sum = 0.0
    66|            var count = 0
    67|            for (i in 0 until binFrequencies.size) {
    68|                val freq = binFrequencies[i]
    69|                if (freq >= lower && freq <= upper) {
    70|                    if (magnitudesDb[i] > noiseFloorDb) {
    71|                        sum += magnitudesDb[i]
    72|                        count++
    73|                    }
    74|                }
    75|                if (freq > upper) break
    76|            }
    77|            bandLevels[b] = if (count > 0) (sum / count).toFloat() else noiseFloorDb
    78|        }

    80|        currentBandLevels = bandLevels
    81|        return bandLevels
    82|    }
    83|
    84|    /**
    85|     * Compute correction gains by comparing measured bands to reference bands.
    86|     *
    87|     * Fast two-band mode: at most twice per second, the two most deviant bands
    88|     * get corrected simultaneously — the band that most exceeds its target
    89|     * (highest deviation, cut) and the one that most lacks (lowest deviation,
    90|     * boost). All other bands keep their current gain.
    91|     *
    92|     * @param referenceLevels dB per band from the source signal
    93|     * @param measuredLevels dB per band from the microphone
    94|     * @param currentBands existing EQ bands (for smooth transitions)
    95|     * @return updated list of EqBand with new target gains
    96|     */
    97|    fun computeCorrections(
    98|        referenceLevels: FloatArray,
    99|        measuredLevels: FloatArray,
   100|        currentBands: List<EqBand>
   101|    ): List<EqBand> {
   102|        val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
   103|        if (now - lastCorrectionMs < TWO_BAND_PERIOD_MS) {
   104|            return currentBands
   105|        }
   106|        lastCorrectionMs = now
   107|
   108|        if (currentBands.isEmpty()) return currentBands
   109|
   110|        // Deviation per band: how much the room boosts (+) or dips (−) it
   111|        var maxIdx = -1
   112|        var minIdx = -1
   113|        for (i in currentBands.indices) {
   114|            val refLevel = if (i < referenceLevels.size) referenceLevels[i] else 0f
   115|            val measLevel = if (i < measuredLevels.size) measuredLevels[i] else 0f
   116|            val deviation = measLevel - refLevel

   118|            if (minIdx == -1 || deviation < deviationAt(minIdx, referenceLevels, measuredLevels)) minIdx = i
   119|        }
   120|
   121|        val result = currentBands.toMutableList()

   123|            val d = deviationAt(maxIdx, referenceLevels, measuredLevels)
   124|            result[maxIdx] = applyCorrection(result[maxIdx], maxIdx, -d)
   125|        }

   128|            result[minIdx] = applyCorrection(result[minIdx], minIdx, -d)
   129|        }
   130|        return result
   131|    }
   132|
   133|    private fun deviationAt(i: Int, referenceLevels: FloatArray, measuredLevels: FloatArray): Float {
   134|        val refLevel = if (i < referenceLevels.size) referenceLevels[i] else 0f
   135|        val measLevel = if (i < measuredLevels.size) measuredLevels[i] else 0f
   136|        return measLevel - refLevel
   137|    }
   138|
   139|    /** Clamp, smooth and store the correction for a single band. */
   140|    private fun applyCorrection(band: EqBand, index: Int, rawCorrection: Float): EqBand {

   147|    /**

   149|     */
   150|    fun applyGainsToSpectrum(
   151|        spectrum: SpectrumFrame,
   152|        bands: List<EqBand>
   153|    ): SpectrumFrame {
   154|        val corrected = spectrum.magnitudesDb.copyOf()
   155|
   156|        for (band in bands) {
   157|            val center = band.centerFreq
   158|            val gain = band.gainDb

   162|            val bandwidth = center / q
   163|            for (i in spectrum.frequencies.indices) {
   164|                val freq = spectrum.frequencies[i]
   165|                val distance = abs(log10(freq / center.toDouble()))

   167|                    val taper = (1.0 - distance / log10(bandwidth / center + 1.0)).toFloat()

   180|     */

The user says: the two bands to correct per cycle are not the ones with highest/lowest Hz — they are the bands with the highest and lowest measured SPL dB, then the next two, etc.

Looking at my RoomCorrector implementation: I select maxIdx/minIdx by deviation (measured - reference). But the user seems to perceive it's picking by frequency. Actually the current logic picks by deviation which is close to "highest/lowest dB relative to target". But the user wants: the band with highest measured SPL (above target) gets cut, and the band with lowest measured SPL gets boosted — considering absolute measured dB, and importantly: "Y después la siguientes dos" — after correcting a pair, move to the NEXT two (rotating through bands), not always re-selecting the absolute max/min (which would keep hammering the same bands while smoothing lags).

So two changes:
1. Selection criterion: highest measured SPL band (cut) and lowest measured SPL band (boost) — based on measured dB vs reference. Since reference is flat pink noise per band roughly, highest measured = most over target, lowest = most under. But user explicitly says "dbs spl más altos y más bajo" — measured SPL. I'll use measured level (or deviation, which is equivalent if reference is flat — but to follow user literally, use measured levels; yet cutting a band that's loudest in measured terms matches deviation only if reference is flat). Safest: select by measured SPL for both the peak and the dip. Actually correction gain should still use deviation (measured - reference) for how much to cut. Selection: the band with the highest measured SPL → cut; the band with the lowest measured SPL → boost. Hmm, but if reference isn't flat, cutting the loudest measured band might not be right. But user explicitly asked. Pink noise per-band reference should be roughly flat. I'll select by measured level.

2. "Y después la siguientes dos" — rotate: keep a pointer/round-robin. After correcting pair k, next cycle corrects the next pair. Implementation: maintain an index cursor. Each cycle, among remaining bands (ordered by SPL?), pick... Simplest faithful implementation: keep a `correctionCursor` that advances each cycle. Each cycle:
- Find the highest-SPL band and lowest-SPL band starting the search from the cursor position (wrapping), so subsequent cycles pick different bands.
- Advance cursor by 2 (past those indices).

Alternative interpretation: every cycle picks the current highest & lowest measured, but since smoothing is gradual, the same bands would be picked repeatedly until corrected — which is arguably correct behavior ("la más alta y la más baja desviadas"). But the user says "Y después la siguientes dos" — after this pair, the next two. That suggests round-robin: cycle 1 fixes bands A(highest) & B(lowest), cycle 2 fixes the next highest & next lowest, etc., sweeping through all bands, then repeat.

I'll implement a cursor over bands sorted... Simpler: a rotating index `nextBandIndex`. Each cycle:
- i1 = band with max measured SPL among all bands starting from nextBandIndex (wrap)
- i2 = band with min measured SPL among all bands starting from nextBandIndex (wrap), excluding i1
- apply corrections
- nextBandIndex = (highest index found + 1) % bandCount — or just advance by 2 from current cursor: nextBandIndex = (nextBandIndex + 2) % bandCount.

Using a window search from cursor: each cycle, search over a "window" — but the user wants "the highest and lowest, then the next two". That means ordering bands by SPL descending? Or by index? "Las que tengan los dbs spl más altos y más bajo. Y después las siguientes dos" — the pair (highest, lowest), then the following pair (second highest, second lowest)? Or next two in sequence?

Most sensible audio interpretation: cycle 1 corrects the loudest band (cut) and quietest band (boost); cycle 2 corrects the next loudest and next quietest; and so on — a sweep through deviations by rank. After all bands have been touched, restart from rank 1.

Implementation with rank sweep:
- Keep a `rankCursor` (int, increments by 1 each cycle, resets when exceeding bandCount).
- Cycle: cutIdx = band with rankCursor-th highest measured SPL (excluding recently corrected? no); boostIdx = band with rankCursor-th lowest measured SPL.
- If cutIdx == boostIdx, pick alternative.

edits.oldString:
/**
     * Compute correction gains by comparing measured bands to reference bands.
     *
     * Fast two-band mode: at most twice per second, the two most deviant bands
     * get corrected simultaneously — the band that most exceeds its target
     * (highest deviation, cut) and the one that most lacks (lowest deviation,
     * boost). All other bands keep their current gain.
     *
     * @param referenceLevels dB per band from the source signal
     * @param measuredLevels dB per band from the microphone
     * @param currentBands existing EQ bands (for smooth transitions)
     * @return updated list of EqBand with new target gains
     */
    fun computeCorrections(
        referenceLevels: FloatArray,
        measuredLevels: FloatArray,
        currentBands: List<EqBand>
    ): List<EqBand> {
        val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
        if (now - lastCorrectionMs < TWO_BAND_PERIOD_MS) {
            return currentBands
        }
        lastCorrectionMs = now

        if (currentBands.isEmpty()) return currentBands

        // Deviation per band: how much the room boosts (+) or dips (−) it
        var maxIdx = -1
        var minIdx = -1
        for (i in currentBands.indices) {
            val refLevel = if (i < referenceLevels.size) referenceLevels[i] else 0f
            val measLevel = if (i < measuredLevels.size) measuredLevels[i] else 0f
            val deviation = measLevel - refLevel
            if (maxIdx == -1 || deviation > deviationAt(maxIdx, referenceLevels, measuredLevels)) maxIdx = i
            if (minIdx == -1 || deviation < deviationAt(minIdx, referenceLevels, measuredLevels)) minIdx = i
        }

        val result = currentBands.toMutableList()
        if (maxIdx >= 0) {
            val d = deviationAt(maxIdx, referenceLevels, measuredLevels)
            result[maxIdx] = applyCorrection(result[maxIdx], maxIdx, -d)
        }
        if (minIdx >= 0 && minIdx != maxIdx) {
            val d = deviationAt(minIdx, referenceLevels, measuredLevels)
            result[minIdx] = applyCorrection(result[minIdx], minIdx, -d)
        }
        return result
    }

Corregido y compilado ✔. Ahora la auto-corrección funciona así:

1. **Ranking por SPL medido**: cada 500 ms se ordenan todas las bandas por sus dB SPL reales.
2. **Ciclo 1**: se recorta la banda con SPL **más alto** y se sube la de SPL **más bajo**, a la vez.
3. **Ciclo siguiente**: pasa a las **siguientes dos** del ranking (2ª más alta + 2ª más baja), y así sucesivamente — barrido rotativo.
4. Cuando todas las bandas fueron tocadas, el barrido **se reinicia desde arriba**, tomando de nuevo los niveles ya corregidos.

La magnitud de cada corte/subida sigue siendo la desviación respecto a la referencia, con clamp al límite configurado (hasta 50 dB) y suavizado adaptativo. Al reiniciar la corrección (botón reset), el barrido también vuelve a empezar de cero.

Pruébalo en el simulador y luego en tu Redmi — si notas que el barrido va demasiado rápido o lento, te ajusto la cadencia.

Así se equilibra el sonido de forma más precisa y natural.
